title: Dedekind independence of multiplicative characters
statement: Let $M$ be a monoid (a set with an associative multiplication and a two-sided identity $1$), and let $L$ be a field [def-weil-field]. Let $n\geq 0$ and let $\chi_1,\ldots,\chi_n:M\to L$ be pairwise distinct monoid homomorphisms, where $L$ has its multiplicative monoid structure: $\chi_j(1)=1$ and $\chi_j(xy)=\chi_j(x)\chi_j(y)$. Then these functions are $L$-linearly independent. Explicitly, if $\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_n\in L$ and $\sum_{j=1}^n\lambda_j\chi_j(x)=0$ for every $x\in M$, then every $\lambda_j$ is zero.

mathlib_match.how: specializes in one line: at Basic.lean:498--499 the family of all monoid homomorphisms into any commutative domain is linearly independent over that domain; restrict this family to the injective finite list of distinct characters and specialize the domain to the field L. The explicit finite-relation formulation is the definition of linear independence.
